title: Gröbner Bases for General Polynomial Systems over Zq
summary: Gröbner-basis techniques solve uniquely solvable overdetermined systems over Zq at higher cost than over finite fields, but their applicability to more general systems remains open.

formal_statement.body: For polynomial systems over $\mathbb{Z}_q$, Grobner-basis techniques can solve overdetermined systems that admit a unique solution, although at higher cost than when solving such systems over finite fields; determine whether, and under what conditions, Grobner-basis methods can find solutions to more general polynomial systems over $\mathbb{Z}_q$.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of polynomial systems over the ring Zq using Gröbner-basis techniques.
assumptions: The known solvable case is overdetermined.
The known solvable case admits a unique solution.
parameters: q determines the coefficient ring Zq
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether, and under what conditions, Gröbner-basis methods can find solutions to more general polynomial systems over Zq.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of Symmetric Primitives over Rings and a Key Recovery Attack on Rubato

progress.summary: The source presents uniquely solvable overdetermined systems as tractable by Gröbner-basis techniques, though at higher cost than over finite fields. It explicitly identifies applicability to more general systems over Zq as open.
citation_labels: Lorenzo Grassi et al., Cryptanalysis of Symmetric Primitives over Rings and a Key Recovery Attack on Rubato
